# Independent audit: unframed rank-stratum hinge normality

Source: `candidate da91e18223378a53`.
**PASS**, with the original cap count retained and outside-source
contacts explicitly allowed.

## Minimal normal face and local parameterization

The smallest face containing zero is exposed by a linear functional
vanishing on that face and strictly positive on the other listed normals.
Every balanced nonnegative relation therefore uses only that face. Its
caps already supply every whole-space covering certificate. A
positive-hinge cap outside the face could be replaced by an empty cap
without changing coverage, contradicting global minimality. Thus every
replaced cap has zero hinge and zero source mass.

Replacing those caps by empty caps with unit normals in the face span
preserves the attained value, budgets, and exact cap count. The span has
positive dimension; zero cannot be a vertex of the convex hull of unit
normals. The surviving normal convex hull contains a relative ball about
zero. This positive spanning persists under nearby variations within
the span, and supplies local coercivity and a fixed local compact cube
for the coverage LP.

The `SO(d) x product S(V)` parameterization is smooth despite its
redundancy. Whole-space coverage is exactly independent of the common
rotation, and the uniform offset repair stays in this parameter space.
Every local competitor is also a competitor for the original unrestricted
problem, so the global semialgebraic value function supplies the needed
penalty bound. No unproved regularity of a new rank-restricted value is
used. The normal objective coefficient and exact total budget sensitivity
therefore follow from the already audited penalty proof.

## Consistent derivatives and the full tensor

Applying the smooth pullback rule to each physical cap-mass function
allows the individual-normal and common-rotation components to use one
consistent section measure. This avoids an invalid choice of independent
facet traces in different parameter directions. The local coverage LP's
contacts lie inside its artificial cube, so each saddle relation has zero
continuous resultant. These contacts lie in the normal span, but need
not lie in the source fiber.

Offset and base variations give the stated all-cap mass and base moment
equations. Individual sphere variations within the span give the
projected continuous equation, including in rank one, where the sphere
has zero-dimensional tangent space. Its radial multiplier is fixed by
the cap, section, and contact Euler identities.

For `T=sum_i (X_i+r_i X_i^s)u_i^T`, the projected equations give
`P_V T=Q`, and the normals give `T=T P_V`. Common rotations have no
coverage derivative and yield zero pairing of `T` with every
skew-symmetric matrix, so `T` is symmetric. These three facts give
`T=Q` in the full continuous ambient space. No missing perpendicular
component remains. The right side is a sum of nonnegative multiples
of `u_i u_i^T`, hence positive semidefinite, with trace equal to the
hinge objective.

The regression consequence uses the labeled cap-plus-section measure,
including its actual section second moments. Null directions of the
affine-base Gram matrix annihilate the cross moments. After regression,
the cross moment with the normal label remains `Q`. The block
second-moment matrix is positive semidefinite, and minimizing its
quadratic form gives `R_x>=Q A^+ Q`. Null directions of `A` annihilate
`Q`, justifying that pseudoinverse as well. The scalar Cauchy--Schwarz
bound has constant one because the normal labels have unit norm.

## Open complements, finite subcovers, and rank one

For the subcover argument, if every subfamily of size at most
`h=2^n(r+1)` failed to cover, choose one strictly complementary point
for each of the finitely many subfamilies. A common continuous cube
contains all witnesses, and a common positive epsilon is smaller than
all their strict margins. The closed halfspaces with margins at most
minus epsilon then satisfy every required small-subfamily feasibility
condition. The proved closed relative Helly lemma applies to
`conv(P)` times that cube, including when the base hull has smaller
affine dimension. Lattice convexity of `P` is exactly the hypothesis
needed to identify its mixed set with `P` times the cube. The resulting
full intersection contradicts whole-space coverage.

Every positive-hinge cap at a global minimizer must belong to any
selected subcover, since an omitted positive-hinge cap could be made
empty. Zero-mass caps are retained in that subcover and contribute zero
to its source union bound; they are not assumed dispensable from the
whole-space cover. Thus the positive-cap count and
`1<=2^n(r+1)tau` follow. For rank one, a strict budget below
`gamma_d/2^n` contradicts this because `2 gamma_d<=1`, including
equality at `d=1`.

The result concerns a selected minimizing representative and its local
rank stratum. It neither places contacts in the source nor excludes
the higher-rank budgets needed for OC.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
